statements.t: Outlook : Various key factors will affect our outcome.
Regarding by-products, we expect to produce 163,400 tonnes of zinc in 2026, which is 1.0% below our initial plan.
We also expect to produce 29,000 tonnes of molybdenum in 2026, which represents an increase of 11.7% compared to our initial plan.
For silver, we expect to comply with our plan to produce 24 million ounces of this metal.

Set forth below are descriptions of some of our current expected capital investment programs.
We expect to meet the cash requirements for these projects by utilizing cash on hand; internally generated funds and additional external financing, including funding received in June 2026.
Our investments in Peruvian projects that are being built or for which basic or detail engineering or environmental studies are being conducted could surpass $10.3 billion in the next decade.
Project update: As of September 30, 2026, the Company has invested $884.3 million in project execution and committed $1,101 million to cover diverse activities, acquisitions and related contracts.
To the extent possible, the Company intends to cover the estimated 7,000 jobs that will be created during Tia Maria’s construction phase with workers from the Islay province.
SCC has several projects in its Mexican pipeline that may boost organic growth if they are found to be of value for both stakeholders and the communities in which we operate.
We have a number of other projects that we may develop in the future.

We continuously evaluate new projects on the basis of our long-term corporate objectives, expected return on investment, environmental concerns, required investment and estimated production, among other considerations.

Project update: Social and environmental management programs are currently being implemented in the communities within the project’s direct area of influence, in accordance with the Framework Agreement signed for the Development of the Tiaparo Peasant Community and the Los Chancas Mining Project.
Regaining control is essential if we are to continue developing our Los Chancas project.
When developed, we expect Michiquillay to produce 225,000 tonnes of copper per year (along with by-products of molybdenum, gold and silver) for an initial mine life of more than 25 years.
We estimate an investment of approximately $2.5 billion will be required and expect production start-up by 2032.
In this context, our project’s initiation is dependent on action at the Mexican government level.

Additional projects in the Mexican pipeline are Angangueo and Chalchihuites (which are part of the Mexican copper circuit) and the Empalme Smelter, which are expected to bolster our position as a fully integrated copper producer.
We cannot make any assurances that we will undertake any of these projects or that the information noted is accurate.

As part of our commitment to promote stakeholders’ active participation in new project development, the Participative Environmental Committee for the Michiquillay project in Peru completed its third verification of environmental performance in 2026.
Currently, 17% of the jobs on the Tia Maria project are held by locals, who access these opportunities through our onsite offices or in coordination with local contractors.
We expect to meet the cash requirements for these capital investments from cash on hand, internally generated funds and from additional external financing, including funding received in June 2026.
